findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the empty-scope guard: either add the described `if not scope: return 0` early-return to `_apply_staged_files`, or correct the plan's assertion — as written, `in_repair_scope` returns True on empty scope and `_apply_staged_files` has no guard, so an empty scope copies back every changed file (fail-open).
evidence: Plan quote: 'The guard lives one level up, in `_apply_staged_files`, which returns 0 immediately when `scope` is empty, before it iterates `changed` at all.'
_apply_staged_files (repair.py:184-196) has no `if not scope: return 0`; it loops `for entry in changed` and calls `in_repair_scope(entry, scope)`.
in_repair_scope (ci_repair.py:189-190): `if not scope: return True` — an empty scope matches every changed file, so _apply_staged_files copies back the whole changed set.
findings.finding: The plan asserts _apply_staged_files 'returns 0 immediately when scope is empty, before it iterates changed at all,' but the named implementation file has no such guard: _apply_staged_files iterates changed and delegates to in_repair_scope, which returns True for empty scope, matching every file — the fail-open whole-tree rewrite the ticket claims to remove.
findings.location: Plan: 'Bounding what a fix may write back'; services/orchestration/temporal_activities/repair.py:169-196 and services/orchestration/langgraph/ci_repair.py:189-190
scenarios: A fix command like prettier/npm run lint:fix reformats many files and the failure summary names no path (failing_files returns ()), so scope is empty and every changed file is copied back — the unbounded diff the ticket set out to prevent.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `if not scope: return 0` at the top of _apply_staged_files (before the loop), matching the plan's stated design, so the guarantee does not depend on in_repair_scope's empty-scope return.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the 'empty-scope' outcome reachable and mutually exclusive from 'applied' — this depends on the empty-scope guard actually returning 0, so fix the guard (above) and confirm the discriminator table matches observed behavior.
evidence: Plan quote: 'The seven are mutually exclusive and are evaluated in that order, so every declared outcome is derivable and no two collapse onto the same observation.'

With scope==() , in_repair_scope returns True for every entry (ci_repair.py:189-190), so _apply_staged_files returns len(in-scope changed) > 0 whenever changed_files is non-empty — producing outcome 'applied', not 'empty-scope'.
findings.finding: The Observability table claims the 'empty-scope' outcome is discriminated by failing_files(summary)==() and that the seven outcomes are mutually exclusive, but given the actual in_repair_scope/_apply_staged_files behavior an empty scope yields a non-zero applied count, so 'empty-scope' collapses onto 'applied' and is unreachable.
scenarios: A summary naming no path with a fix that changed files: plan expects 'empty-scope' with 0 applied; code produces 'applied' with the whole changed set.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the default value of `gate_engine_privileged` (recommend false) and how it is set true for the local k3s environment.
evidence: Scope adds gate_engine_privileged but no default is stated.
Grounded assumption: 'Buildah requires privileged: true under k3s on Colima' — implies a non-default environment-specific setting.
findings.finding: The default value and posture of `gate_engine_privileged` is unspecified; the plan adds the config key but never states whether it defaults to false (preserving existing unprivileged runs) or true.
scenarios: An executor sets the default to true and privileged pods run in every environment, or sets it false and the local live-run AC fails without knowing the flag must be flipped.
findings.suggested_fix: Declare `gate_engine_privileged` defaults to false and is opted into per-environment for the local Colima/k3s stack.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the `fix_command` value type (single shell string executed via the pod script builder) and whether shell operators are permitted.
evidence: config/local/checks.yaml.example 'documents the key' but the plan text does not state the value type.
Examples given ('ruff check --fix .', 'prettier --write', 'make fix') mix shell forms.
findings.finding: The `fix_command` config shape (string vs list, and whether it is shell-interpreted) is not specified.
scenarios: An executor must guess whether 'npm run lint:fix && prettier --write' is valid, or whether shell operators are supported, when building the fix script.
findings.suggested_fix: State that fix_command is a single shell command string run inside the same script builder path as the check command.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Capture the privileged-gate-pod decision and its buildah/k3s rationale in an ADR or AGENTS.md update.
evidence: Grounded assumption records the buildah/k3s rationale but is a plan-local note, not a durable design record.
Privileged pods are a cross-component security capability.
findings.finding: Introducing privileged gate pods is a notable security-posture change threaded through gates/pod_runner, gates/builtin, and checks; the buildah rationale is captured in Grounded assumptions but no ADR / AGENTS.md / design-doc update records the decision.
scenarios: A future maintainer removing or auditing the privileged flag has no durable record of why it exists.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Record why rootless buildah with fuse-overlayfs/overlay storage was rejected (or adopt it) rather than defaulting the gate/fix pod to privileged:true, so the security-posture escalation is justified against the documented less-privileged prior art.
evidence: Plan enumerates probes for CAP_SYS_ADMIN and seccomp Unconfined but not fuse-overlayfs/overlay storage; pod uses STORAGE_DRIVER=vfs (gates/pod_runner.py:89)
Retrieved: CERN 'Rootless container builds on Kubernetes' (kubernetes.web.cern.ch/blog/2025/06/19) documents buildah with overlay/fuse-overlayfs storage as the performant rootless path
Retrieved: oneuptime.com 'How to Set Up Buildah for Rootless Container Image Builds' and buildah GH issue #2554 discuss rootless buildah in Kubernetes without privileged access
Granting privileged:true crosses the security/auth bright-line, so a less-privileged established alternative must be weighed before committing
findings.finding: The load-bearing assertion that buildah requires privileged:true under k3s/Colima does not consider the established rootless-buildah alternative (fuse-overlayfs / overlay storage driver), a documented prior-art approach for building images in Kubernetes without a privileged securityContext.
findings.location: Grounded assumptions: 'Buildah requires privileged: true under k3s on Colima, confirmed by four probe pods. CAP_SYS_ADMIN alone, and with seccomp Unconfined, both fail...'; AC line granting 'the gate pod runs privileged'
scenarios: Deploying the gate/fix pod to a multi-tenant or hardened cluster that forbids privileged pods under Pod Security Standards
Security review objecting to a privileged container running an untrusted project's fix command

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State whether `gate_engine_privileged` must elevate ALL gate/check/scanner pods or only the fix/copy-out path, and if the buildah constraint forces it everywhere, note that the deployment is confined to the single-user local Colima/k3s stack (flag off by default, no SA token) so the escape blast radius stays bounded.
evidence: Plan Scope: 'gates/pod_runner.py gains a privileged flag ... scripts/config.py gains gate_engine_privileged. gates/builtin.py, temporal_activities/checks.py, and temporal_workflows/draft_pull_request.py thread them through.'

Verified in repo: `privileged=settings.gate_engine_privileged` appears in services/orchestration/temporal_activities/checks.py:71, gates/builtin.py:173, gates/scanner_pod.py:166, and temporal_activities/repair.py:139 — one global switch, all pods.
scripts/config.py:130 `gate_engine_privileged: bool = False` (opt-in default).
pod_runner.py:82 `automountServiceAccountToken: False` — no k8s API token exposed to the privileged pod.
All non-codebase ACs carry provenance environment=local-colima-k3s; principal=joeoakhart; privilege_posture=broader — single-user local stack, not multi-tenant/internet-reachable.
findings.finding: The single `gate_engine_privileged` flag the plan threads through elevates every gate, check, and scanner pod, not just the new fix/copy-out path, so enabling it to satisfy the fix use-case simultaneously runs all lower-trust repo content (fix_command plus check scripts) in a privileged (container-escape-capable) pod. This is a least-privilege breadth concern; it is advisory because the declared deployment is a single-user local Colima/k3s stack with the flag defaulted off and no service-account token mounted.
findings.location: Scope — gates/pod_runner.py privileged flag; scripts/config.py gate_engine_privileged; threaded via checks.py, builtin.py, scanner_pod.py, repair.py
scenarios: An operator enables gate_engine_privileged for the fix path; every subsequent check/scanner pod running an untrusted repo's toolchain now runs privileged, widening escape surface beyond the fix use-case that motivated the flag.
The platform is later pointed at a less-trusted or shared cluster where the private-stack assumption no longer holds.
